      "observations": [
        "The patch splits one regular-position file into three size-slice files and one duration file into four single-size files. It moves duration cases into shared head.js and lowers the shared timeout multiplier from8to3. Setup/data and ordered per-scenario calls remain shared; this is a file workload split, not proof of faster or reliable tests.",
        "The actual regular-position calls use sizes.slice(0,2),slice(3,5),slice(6,9), leaving indices2and5 out of those three entrypoints. The four duration files exercise sizes0–3 with durations3,6,12,24,36,72,144; they do not restore the complete old regular duration1 matrix for indices2/5. Fixed source preserves the same slices. This is a bounded static coverage difference; it does not prove no other test covers these sizes or a product geometry defect.",
        "Each position scenario creates an event and checks four geometry predicates for each scroll position, then closes the dialog and removes the event. resizeWindow uses a resize debounce plus fallback timeout and frame wait; that existing helper is not a new general permission for arbitrary sleeps. Current setup also removes its injected style through cleanup.",
        "Review initial split/lower timeout still failed. Author proposed raising the shared timeout, then split the second file instead and reported four debug/ccov runs without failure. Bug records a proposed full backout that was not done because of interleaved changes; no all-tests-passing result is inferred.",
        "The reviewer objected to an underscore-prefixed parameter that was used, suggesting winSizes. The actual source uses windowSizes, which resolves the local global-name conflict without adopting that exact spelling. No global naming rule is inferred."
      ],
